items.tx:
This is incredibly alarming and especially disturbing of the German police. To give into terrorist threats from the Islamic Republic in Iran is to accept the silencing of your own nation. 

What’s even worse is that Germany is a democracy. One of the most vital pieces of a democracy is the right to self-expression and freedom of speech. 

Unbelievable. During this time, it’s crucial we support Reza Pahlavi and his family. Along the streets of Iran, blood continues to spill into drains of crushed dreams. All for supporting the exiled Crown Prince. Even Iranian people refused to be silenced when their own lives are on the line.

So why is Germany, a democracy, willing to give in like this?

qt.t:
Yasmine Pahlavi said Friday that German police had informed her and her husband, Reza Pahlavi, the exiled Crown Prince of Iran, that they would not be allowed to attend or address a rally in Frankfurt on Saturday because of threats from the Islamic Republic.

She said police warned that Tehran could retaliate by targeting people in the crowd if her husband attended. The exiled Crown Prince is scheduled to receive a freedom prize in Frankfurt on behalf of the Iranian people.

items.t: Iranian exiled Prince Reza Pahlavi plans to attend a gathering of Iranians in Frankfurt, Germany, despite security concerns surrounding his appearance, his com
items.tx:
Iranian exiled Prince Reza Pahlavi plans to attend a gathering of Iranians in Frankfurt, Germany, despite security concerns surrounding his appearance, his communications team said Friday.

In a post on X, his communications team said:

"In response to media inquiries and concerns expressed by our fellow Iranians, we would like to clarify that Prince Reza Pahlavi will still attend the Friedrich Naumann Freedom Award ceremony and is determined to join the large gathering of Iranians at Frankfurt's Ostpark afterward.

"The gathering will proceed as scheduled, and the Prince's team is working closely with security authorities and police to make every effort to facilitate his attendance."

qt.t:
Frankfurt police have told Iranian exiled Prince Reza Pahlavi and his wife Yasmine that they cannot attend or address a rally because of threats of violence from the Islamic Republic, she said in a statement.

Yasmine Pahlavi said her husband would be in Frankfurt on Saturday to accept the Freedom Prize on behalf of the Iranian people, but police had informed the couple they would prevent them from attending the rally.

“The police have told us that if my husband attends, the Islamic Republic may retaliate by targeting innocent people in the crowd,” she said.

Frankfurt police did not immediately respond to Iran International’s request for comment.

Pahlavi said protecting rally participants was essential and expressed respect for law enforcement officers, but questioned whether the restriction reflected political considerations alongside security concerns.

For the first time in its two-decade history, the @FNFreiheit ’s Freedom Prize has been awarded not to an individual, but to an entire nation: the people of Iran.

The prize belongs to the Iranian people. Their struggle will continue until victory.

items.t: MAKE IRAN FREE AGAIN! ✌🏻 I stand with the Iranian people in their aspiration for freedom, democracy and human dignity. @PahlaviReza
My dear compatriots, I have come to Brussels today to bring your message and your demands directly to Europe’s leaders, lawmakers, and public, the voice of a na
items.tx:
My dear compatriots,

I have come to Brussels today to bring your message and your demands directly to Europe’s leaders, lawmakers, and public, the voice of a nation that has stood courageously and steadfastly against the Islamic Republic’s repression and violence, and has refused to surrender to this criminal regime.

In its latest disinformation campaign, the Islamic Republic attempted to prevent you from joining the “Barkhiz Iran” Telegram bot by spreading false information. That effort also failed. Within a short time of its launch, we received hundreds of thousands of messages through the bot from across the country, from students, teachers, and doctors to workers, soldiers, police officers, and people from every walk of life.

We launched this initiative to establish direct, two-way communication with you. The extraordinary response carries a clear message: the will of the Iranian nation cannot be broken.

Our nation, in all its diversity, seeks liberation from the Islamic Republic, and is fighting and making sacrifices to achieve it. The Iranian people do not fear this regime. On the contrary, it is the Islamic Republic that fears the power of a united Iranian nation. It is the regime’s missing leader who is hiding from the people, too afraid even to make his voice heard.

You, my proud compatriots, have once again demonstrated that, contrary to the regime’s propaganda, you are neither exhausted nor hopeless. Your belief in victory is stronger than ever.

I am proud of your courage, resilience, and loyalty to Iran. During the most difficult days, you have remained faithful to your pledge to our homeland. I, too, remain faithful to my pledge to you: to secure Iran’s freedom and restore its pride.

Once again, I call on every compatriot who believes in overthrowing the Islamic Republic and building a free and prosperous future to join the National Cooperation Campaign to Save Iran.

You can communicate directly with my team by scanning the QR code shown during live broadcasts on Iran National Revolution TV and Iran International, or through the Telegram handle BarkhizIranBot.
Be assured that protecting your security is the foremost priority for me and my team throughout this campaign.

For ourselves and future generations, we seek a free, advanced, and proud Iran, an Iran that will once again reclaim its rightful place in the world.

I believe in this future because I believe in you and your unbreakable will. The light of Iran will prevail over the darkness of the Islamic Republic.

Long live Iran.
Reza Pahlavi

items.tx:
Prince Reza Pahlavi’s Opening Remarks at the European Parliament Press Conference – Nov 4, 2026

"Thank you, Mr. Bellamy, for your kind introduction, for hosting us today, and above all for your principled support for the people of Iran.
I am here today with a simple message to Europe: The Islamic Republic is weaker than ever. It will fall. The question is how soon, and whether Europe will stand with the Iranian people or continue to appease this Regime.
In January, millions of courageous Iranians, from every province and every walk of life, rose up against the Islamic Republic.
More than 40,000 Iranians gave their lives for freedom.
Their courage has shaken this regime to its foundations.
It is divided and frightened and under the cover of global silence and promises of appeasement, it is taking its revenge on the people of Iran.
It has discovered how to murder its own people without making international headlines: by executing them one or two at a time. Just two more young men, protesters from the January uprising, were executed yesterday.
Since January, more than 70 political prisoners have reportedly been executed. More than 100 protesters face the threat of execution today. today.
These are hardly even executions. They are state-sponsored murder without basic due process - an attempt to terrorise an entire nation into silence.
But let me be clear: this regime is not just a threat to Iranians. It is a threat to Europe and to the world.
It has supported Putin's brutal war against Ukraine and the destabilization of Europe. It has plotted attacks on European soil and sought to undermine your democracies. It has declared - just a few days ago - your armed forces legitimate targets.
For 47 years, it has exported terrorism, violence and instability.
And for 47 years, the international community has tried to negotiate with it. For 47 years, the international community has failed.
Because the Islamic Republic is not a conventional state that values the welfare of its people. It is a revolutionary jihadist movement that has occupied Iran and turned the country into a headquarters for global terrorism.
There can be no lasting peace or stability in the Middle East while this regime remains in power.
It must go, not just for the people of Iran but also for the interests of Europe.
We are preparing to build a free, stable and prosperous Iran, which will be a partner in trade and security with Europe.
To do so, we have built a broad, unified coalition of the Iranian opposition from left to right, republican and monarchist. I am not here to be the destination, but the bridge to the destination which must be a lasting democracy. The four principles that unite us are simple:
Iran’s territorial integrity
The protection of individual liberties and equality of all citizens;
The Separation of religion and state; and
The Iranian people's right to determine the future democratic form of their government.
Anyone who believes in these principles has room under this tent.
But the Iranian people also need the support of the democratic world.
And today I am calling on the European Union to take four immediate steps. Because as Mr. Bellamy said, Europe should do something and Europe can do something.
First, cut off the regime's networks in Europe.
Expel regime operatives and diplomats abusing their positions. Investigate and act against those facilitating intimidation, money laundering, sanctions evasion and illicit financial activities.
Second, intensify economic and financial pressure.
Apply the same determination you have shown towards PutinPutin. Expose hidden assets and front companies. Freeze illicit wealth. Close the financial networks that sustain the regime and its Revolutionary Guards.
Third, and most urgently, help keep the Iranian people connected to the world.
In January, the regime shut down the internet to hide its atrocities from the world and prevent Iranians from communicating with one another.

items.t: I'm Iranian. I've lived under the Islamic Republic for decades. I've seen how they ruined my country and took away our freedoms and every single right we had. T
items.tx:
I'm Iranian. I've lived under the Islamic Republic for decades. I've seen how they ruined my country and took away our freedoms and every single right we had.

They control what you can wear, what music you can listen to, how you behave in public, and even how men and women are allowed to interact. Women are forced to follow a dress code. Women can't even sing solo in public. Dancing can get you in trouble. Drinking alcohol is illegal. Having a private party with men and women together can get your home raided and everyone arrested. Relationships outside marriage are criminalized. Even what you can watch, listen to, say, and post online is subject to censorship. Social media platforms are blocked. You can be punished, imprisoned, or even executed for speaking out against the regime.

Your own home isn't necessarily safe from their interference. Your private life isn't yours. Your freedom isn't yours. They want to dictate how you live, from the moment you wake up to the moment you go to sleep.

This is the country I grew up in. This is what I experienced. They took so much from me that I was eventually forced to flee my own country.

America, I'm terrified for you. I know exactly where this road leads. I've watched it. I lived it. https://x.com/JustinUSA/status/2117872101138866480/video/1

items.tx:
🇶🇦 Qatar is the Islamic Republic’s hardest-working diplomatic advocate because the regime keeps Iran weak and poor while making Qatar rich.

Qatar's interest lies beneath the Persian Gulf, where Qatar and Iran control different sections of the world’s largest shared natural-gas reservoir.

The field covers approximately 9,700 square kilometres:

▪️ Qatar’s North Field: 6,000 km², or 62%.
▪️ Iran’s South Pars: 3,700 km², or 38%.

The estimated recoverable reserves are equally divided in Qatar’s favour:

▪️ Qatar: approximately 900 trillion cubic feet.
▪️ Iran: approximately 360 trillion cubic feet.

There is no joint development agreement. Each side extracts independently from the same connected reservoir, making investment, technology and production capacity strategically important.

Qatar used Western technology and capital to build an LNG empire from its share. Before the recent conflict, it possessed approximately 77 million tonnes of annual LNG capacity and exported more than 80 million tonnes in 2025.

Its expansion plans aim to increase capacity to approximately 126 million tonnes annually, eventually reaching 142 million tonnes around 2030.

The Islamic Republic built nothing comparable.

South Pars supplies approximately 70–75% of Iran’s gas, but almost all of it is consumed domestically for electricity, heating, industry and petrochemicals. Iran possesses essentially no LNG export capacity and remains constrained by sanctions, corruption, pressure decline and technological isolation.

Qatar transformed its share into global wealth and influence while the Islamic Republic left Iranians facing shortages and blackouts above the same reservoir.

A competent post-regime government could attract Western investment, install urgently needed compression infrastructure, construct LNG terminals and turn Iran into a direct competitor in the same markets Qatar dominates.

That would threaten the foundation of Qatar’s wealth.

Qatar does not want another war damaging its LNG facilities or disrupting the Strait of Hormuz. But it also has powerful reasons to oppose the emergence of a free, stable and economically competitive Iran.

Its preferred outcome is preservation without empowerment. Keep the Islamic Republic alive, keep Iran sanctioned and keep South Pars commercially restrained.

Qatar then converts the resulting gas wealth into political leverage. It hosts a major American military base and invests heavily throughout the West while sheltering Hamas leaders, supporting Muslim Brotherhood networks and financing Islamist-linked institutions abroad.

Al Jazeera supplies the influence platform. Qatar backs disruptive actors, maintains relationships with hostile movements and then presents itself as the indispensable mediator capable of negotiating with them.

This is not a contradiction. It is the strategy.

Gas wealth finances influence. Islamist networks create leverage. Mediation protects Qatar and makes other governments dependent on its access.

The emir’s appeal to President Trump is therefore not selfless diplomacy. It protects Qatar’s LNG infrastructure, political influence and profitable advantage over Iran.

Qatar does not need the Islamic Republic to become powerful. It needs the regime alive enough to prevent Iran from becoming powerful.

items.tx:
Remember this week.

This is where the Iran war stopped being a Middle East war.

Iran's army: if Iran is attacked again, it will hit ALL American assets "without regard to any geographical restrictions."
An Iranian MP on parliament's security committee: "If America uses its bases in Europe, including in Italy and Germany, Iran's missiles will be fired towards Europe."
Tehran's Hamshahri newspaper: a map of 15 potential military targets in 9 European countries.
🇬🇧 🇩🇪 🇫🇷 🇮🇹 🇬🇷 🇷🇴 🇦🇱 🇵🇹 🇨🇾
Iran-linked ships: at least 4 caught slowing, looping and going dark over undersea internet cables in the Gulf of Oman, next to Hormuz.
Brent crude: from about $93.5 yesterday to briefly above $100 this morning.

The same MP said it out loud: "In the two previous wars we did not do this."

Strip out the noise and one thing is left:

Europe is no longer outside this war. By Iran's own words, the moment a US strike leaves a base in Italy or Germany, Europe stops being a bystander. It becomes a target.

Windward, the maritime data firm that tracked those ships, says the pattern fits mapping cable routes or potentially placing charges or mines. 6 cables run under Hormuz. Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar get their internet ONLY through them.

And Trump on Iran, last night: "I would rather not destroy the rest of the country if possible, but maybe I'll have to. You will know soon enough."

The front line now runs from the seabed off Hormuz to the US bases in Europe.

Share this so people in Italy, Germany and Britain see it, and follow me for every update.
